question: In an emergency, how should riders be allowed to exit a bus?
explanation: The manual states drivers should "Allow riders to exit by any window or door in an emergency."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, general safety guidance (p. 4-1)

question: What document shows which materials are considered hazardous for transportation purposes?
explanation: The manual states, "The Federal Hazardous Materials Table shows which materials are hazardous. They pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.1 Hazardous Materials

question: According to the manual, how many different four-inch, diamond-shaped hazard labels are there?
explanation: The manual states, "There are nine different four-inch, diamond-shaped hazard labels."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.1 Hazardous Materials

question: Which of the following is a hazardous material the manual says buses must never carry?
explanation: The list of materials buses must never carry includes "Division 2.3 poison gas, liquid Class 6 poison, tear gas, irritating material."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.2 Forbidden Hazardous Materials

question: Buses must never carry more than how many pounds of solid Class 6 poisons?
explanation: The forbidden materials list includes "More than 100 pounds of solid Class 6 poisons."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.2 Forbidden Hazardous Materials

question: Explosives are forbidden in the space occupied by people on a bus, except for what?
explanation: The manual lists as forbidden "Explosives in the space occupied by people, except small arms ammunition."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.2 Forbidden Hazardous Materials

question: When hazardous materials are allowed on a bus, what are the total and per-class weight limits stated in the manual?
choice_a: 100 pounds total, 50 pounds of any one class
choice_b: 500 pounds total, no more than 100 pounds of any one class
choice_c: 1,000 pounds total, no more than 200 pounds of any one class
choice_d: There is no weight limit as long as materials are labeled
explanation: The manual permits "More than 500 pounds total of allowed hazardous materials, and no more than 100 pounds of any one class" to be forbidden — meaning the allowed limit is 500 pounds total with no more than 100 pounds of any single class.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.2 Forbidden Hazardous Materials

question: If a rider tries to board with an unlabeled hazardous material such as a car battery or gasoline, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Do not allow riders to carry on such common hazards
choice_b: Allow it if the rider promises it's safe
choice_c: Charge an extra fee and allow it
choice_d: Store it in the luggage compartment away from riders
explanation: The manual warns, "Riders sometimes board a bus with an unlabeled hazardous material. Do not allow riders to carry on common hazards such as car batteries or gasoline."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.2 Forbidden Hazardous Materials

question: What is a "standee line" on a bus?
choice_a: The line where riders wait to board the bus
choice_b: The boundary of the luggage compartment
choice_c: A line marking where riders may not stand, forward of the rear of the driver's seat
choice_d: The painted line separating bus lanes on the road
explanation: The manual states, "No rider may stand forward of the rear of the driver's seat... This is called the standee line. All standing riders must stay behind it."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.3 Standee Line

question: On buses designed to allow standing, the floor marking (or other means of showing riders where they cannot stand) is typically what?
explanation: The manual states such buses "must have a two-inch line on the floor or some other means of showing riders where they cannot stand."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.3 Standee Line

question: When arriving at a destination or intermediate stop, the manual says drivers should announce all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_b: The names of all passengers on board
choice_d: Next departure time and bus number
explanation: The manual lists announcements of the location, reason for stopping, next departure time, and bus number — it does not mention announcing passenger names.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.4 At Your Destination

question: If the aisle is on a lower level than the seats, when is it best to remind riders of the step-down?
choice_a: Before coming to a complete stop
choice_b: After the bus has come to a complete stop
explanation: The manual advises, "If the aisle is on a lower level than the seats, remind riders of the step-down. It is best to tell them before coming to a complete stop."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.4 At Your Destination

question: Why does the manual say charter bus drivers should not allow riders on the bus until departure time?
choice_a: To comply with a fuel economy rule
choice_c: To help prevent theft or vandalism of the bus
choice_d: To ensure the air conditioning has time to run
explanation: The manual states, "Charter bus drivers should not allow riders on the bus until departure time. This will help prevent theft or vandalism of the bus."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.2.4 At Your Destination

question: While driving, what does the manual instruct a bus driver to scan?
choice_b: The interior of the bus as well as the road ahead, to the sides, and to the rear
choice_d: Only the fuel and temperature gauges
explanation: The manual states, "While driving, scan the interior of your bus as well as the road ahead, to the sides, and to the rear."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.1 Passenger Supervision

question: What does the manual say drivers should do to avoid rider injury when starting and stopping the bus?
choice_a: Accelerate quickly to stay on schedule
choice_c: Only worry about braking, not starting
choice_d: Start and stop as smoothly as possible, and wait for riders to sit or brace themselves
explanation: The manual states, "Wait for them to sit down or brace themselves before starting. Starting and stopping should be as smooth as possible to avoid rider injury."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.2 At Stops

question: If a driver has a drunk or disruptive rider who must be discharged, where does the manual say it may be safer to do so?
choice_c: At the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area with other people
explanation: The manual states, "Don't discharge such riders where it would be unsafe for them. It may be safer at the next scheduled stop or a well-lighted area where there are other people."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.2 At Stops

question: If your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve, what does the manual say this indicates?
explanation: The manual states, "If your bus leans toward the outside on a banked curve, you are driving too fast."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.4 Speed on Curves

question: At a railroad crossing, how far before the crossing should a bus driver stop?
explanation: The manual states, "Stop your bus between 15 and 50 feet before railroad crossings."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.5 Railroad-highway Crossing/Stops

question: Why might a driver open the forward door when stopped at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: To let passengers exit if needed
choice_c: It is required at every crossing regardless of visibility
choice_d: If it improves the driver's ability to see or hear an approaching train
explanation: The manual states, "You should open your forward door if it improves your ability to see or hear an approaching train."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.5 Railroad-highway Crossing/Stops

question: If a bus has a manual transmission, what should the driver never do while crossing railroad tracks?
explanation: The manual states, "If your bus has a manual transmission, never change gears while crossing the tracks."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.5 Railroad-highway Crossing/Stops

question: At which of the following does a driver NOT need to stop at a railroad crossing, but must still slow down and carefully check for other vehicles?
choice_a: A crossing where a stop sign controls traffic
choice_d: A crossing without visible warning signs
explanation: The manual lists crossings where a driver does not have to stop but must slow down and check, including "At crossings marked as 'exempt' or 'abandoned.'"
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.5 Railroad-highway Crossing/Stops

question: A bus driver must stop at least how many feet before the draw of a drawbridge that lacks a signal light or traffic control attendant?
explanation: The manual states, "Stop at least 50 feet before the draw of the bridge."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.3.6 Drawbridges

question: If a driver works for an interstate carrier, what must be completed after inspecting the bus at the end of a shift?
choice_a: A verbal report to the next driver only
choice_b: A photograph of the bus exterior
choice_c: Nothing, unless a defect is found
choice_d: A written inspection report listing any safety-related defects
explanation: The manual states, "If you work for an interstate carrier, you must complete a written inspection report for each bus driven. The report must specify each bus and list any defect that would affect safety or result in a breakdown."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.4 After-trip Vehicle Inspection

question: What does the manual say about fueling a bus with riders on board?
choice_b: Avoid it unless absolutely necessary, and never refuel in a closed building with riders aboard
choice_d: There is no restriction on fueling with riders aboard
explanation: The manual states, "Avoid fueling your bus with riders on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel in a closed building with riders on board."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.5 Prohibited Practices

question: Which of the following is listed as a prohibited practice while driving a bus?
choice_c: Talking with riders or engaging in any other distracting activity
explanation: The manual states, "Don't talk with riders, or engage in any other distracting activity, while driving."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.5 Prohibited Practices

question: Under the prohibited practices rules, when may a driver tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard?
choice_a: Only to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers, unless getting off would be unsafe
choice_c: Only if the tow distance is less than one mile
choice_d: Anytime the driver believes it is faster
explanation: The manual states, "Do not tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard the vehicle, unless getting off would be unsafe. Only tow or push the bus to the nearest safe spot to discharge passengers."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.5 Prohibited Practices

question: What does a brake-door interlock system do on urban mass transit coaches equipped with one?
choice_a: Locks the doors when the bus exceeds highway speed
choice_b: Applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open
choice_c: Prevents the engine from starting until doors are closed
explanation: The manual states, "The interlock applies the brakes and holds the throttle in idle position when the rear door is open. The interlock releases when you close the rear door."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.6 Use of Brake-door Interlocks

question: The manual warns that the brake-door interlock safety feature should NOT be used in place of what?
explanation: The manual states, "Do not use this safety feature in place of the parking brake."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 4 - Transporting Passengers Safely, 4.6 Use of Brake-door Interlocks
